summary: This section limits how much money a public company can pay as total managerial remuneration from its net profits. It sets specific percentage caps for different types of directors and provides rules for when a company has no profits or makes inadequate profits. It also requires directors who receive excess payments to refund the money and hold it in trust for the company.
points: Total managerial remuneration by a public company shall not exceed eleven per cent of its net profits.
Remuneration for a single managing director, whole-time director, or manager cannot exceed five per cent of net profits without a special resolution.
If a company has no profits or inadequate profits, remuneration must follow Schedule V.
Any director who receives remuneration in excess of the limits must refund the sum and hold it in trust.
The company cannot waive the recovery of any refundable sum unless approved by a special resolution within two years.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is a public company that earned a net profit during the financial year. The board wants to pay its managing director a remuneration based on the profits. According to the rules, this payment cannot exceed five per cent of the net profits unless the company passes a special resolution in a general meeting to approve a higher amount, while keeping the total remuneration within the overall limits set by the law.

terms.meaning: A director who is entrusted with substantial powers of management of the affairs of the company.
The profits of a company calculated in the manner laid down in section 198.
A resolution passed by a required majority of votes in a general meeting where the intention has been duly specified.
Protecting someone against legal responsibility or financial loss.

watch: Ensure you check whether the company has defaulted on any secured debts, as prior approval from creditors may be needed before the general meeting.
